recent_reviews.author: Bob Davies
recent_reviews.text: The next patients' group meeting is on the 6th of May at 5pm. We established that patients can arrive a little early (say 10 minutes) to discuss individual problems/experience, so the PPG can focus clearly on shared problems. Whether you can attend or not, please write your review, good or bad, and I will continue to bring them to the new team. From the PPG meeting on Feb 4th... The practice is fully staffed for doctors (now at 6, and 6 admin) but doesn't have a practice manager as they're having trouble recruiting because they will also manage the Oldham practice. I have been assured they're wiring up a better fallback after 2 missed calls (most likely you will receive a text that asks you to ring the practice, but I have asked that a bookable slot picker be added too). The website is now 24hr accessible for admin/repeats, but still cannot be used out of office hours to request an appointment. The doctor has concerns about people using it for 'urgent' requests in the middle of the night (when no doctor is available to receive it), I've tried to make a case for it, but if out of hours appointment-requests is a blocker for you, please come to meetings and help me argue the case. I have also reraised when tests come back all green, but you're still sick, the practice currently close your diagnosis process until you re-engage (which you may not be told you need to do), which I intend to reraise in future. --- From the PPG meeting on November 26th... 2 new doctors are on board, and new staff are coming soon. Complaints about reception seem to be improving, less reliance on agency staff. The website will be switched to 24hr accessible. New Bank is on Bookable, which is much easier to use and is currently accessible outside of office hours (unlike PATCHS), but doesn't work for existing registered patients, and only has a limited number of slots and is only for booking an appointment. --- From the PPG meeting on 10th of September. The practice is moving to a new digital system on 1st of October, which 'should' solve some of the current technical issues with arranging appointments. Management say there will be some onboarding help and open/group sessions for anybody who would like to attend, and dates/times of those will be on a notice-board in the reception (or from Lynne, the operations manager) once those dates are arranged (probably a couple of evenings/saturdays depending on demand). We have also been assurred the quality of help from reception has been better in the last month and will continue to improve. There is still no new practice manager. They are recruiting for one in a difficult market, but they are adding new administrators (from October 6th, if I understood correctly) and _should_ soon be adding extra doctors too, with a less clear timescale (presumably notice-period related). The patient load on doctors is within the normal NHS range, so do not put off making an appointment just because you think they're busy, they have capacity and are adding more, and most of the problems seem to be steadily improving. --- After leaving a previous 1 star review with many negative points and being frustrated with being unable to arrange an appointment, I attended the newly set-up Patient Participation Group meeting (as a new management company took over in April) on 6th August. The discussion between the team and a few patients was constructive and the new management team seem to have an understanding of the problems after we explained in some detail. I also brought these reviews to their attention, and provided a breakdown of reviews to their management in the meeting. If you're here because you've had a negative experience, either recently or before the take-over, we've been assured they're working on it and should be moving to a new system, as well as dealing with the problems caused by specific staff. Please contact management with feedback and come to the patient meeting if you have the time, be heard, the new team are (it seems) finally listening, and they actually have a mandate to fix problems atm.

recent_reviews.author: Ken Kamdy
recent_reviews.text: A call was initiated to ascertain why an appointment for a mother and child was declined by a GP, providing clinical advice to the service user, and you are not part of the medical team. NHS staff must not unreasonably deny access to services, and patients are entitled to be treated with dignity, receive clear information, and file a formal complaint regarding inadequate care or discourteous conduct. However, a staff member and a receptionist unjustly canceled an appointment, and I have requested the call log. Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. It is unfortunate that this matter is not being addressed; I intend to escalate this issue further due to the appalling service.

recent_reviews.author: Fiona Simpson
recent_reviews.text: I am always really happy with and satisfied with all interactions with the surgery, and actually recommend it to others. The 2 main doctors and advanced clinician are always very good and are through, listen and take concerns seriously. The patches system is very good and easy to use - myself and spouse have had to use it a few times recently, and we have always then been contacted with an appropriate appointment, if that was face to face, urgent phone, or routine that has always happened quickly. There are some people complaining about lack of appointments etc, I have never found this to be the case. I work in primary care and regularly deal with different GP surgeries, and believe me, simpson medical are one of the better ones!! Perhaps everyone needs to have realistic expectations, and consider that there is high demand for healthcare, which exceeds capacity. The old days of face to face appointments are gone, unless it is necessary this does not happen anymore - often phone calls, including photos etc are often sufficent, and more a more efficient use of staff resources. If a face to face appointment is necessary it will be made whilst anything regarding mental health has always been taking seriously and urgently. I am very happy with being a patient here, and think given the demand they do a good job, and are one of the better surgeries I deal with. Thank you to the staff, I appreciate it

recent_reviews.author: Hamaad Farooq
recent_reviews.text: I visited the surgery today while in severe pain and was told my prescription would be sent to the pharmacy. I went to the pharmacy but the prescription had not been sent. I returned after one hour and it was still not there. When I called the surgery, the receptionist told me to wait another hour while they checked with the doctor. When someone is in severe pain and unable to drive, delays like this are extremely frustrating and unacceptable. The doctor was kind and helpful, but the communication and urgency from reception staff needs serious improvement. What is also frustrating is that when staff are rude it seems to be accepted, but when a patient in severe pain becomes frustrated it is quickly labelled as “abuse.” Patients deserve to be treated with understanding and respect, especially when they are in pain and asking for urgent help.

recent_reviews.author: Philip Crossley
recent_reviews.text: Lottery appointment system, You need to call between 8am to 8:30am to win a appointment, but everyone else is also calling at the same time. If your call actually connects during this period, congratulations you have a ticket that gets you a 30% chance of an appointment ( providing they have not all been taken already) , if not try the lottery again the next day. You have 1/5 chance for an appointment if you follow my advice. I have a hack for those needing urgent doctor, use all the phones you can get access to and call them one after another, one will likely get through. Edit: It is possible now to go into the doctors before 8 am to obtain a golden ( yellow ) ticket, which helps you bypass the lottery phone system and be seen the same day. While the lottery system is not ideal, I can see its a way to deal with a already struggling health system and therefore I am rating this place higher for finding a way to deal with a failing system. (+2 stars )

recent_reviews.author: Alicja Basharyar
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely shocking awful GP. I am diagnosed PCOS patient that just needed a referral for a fertility treatment. After moving to Bolton I registered with this GP hoping for the best knowing I would need a referral as a patient that deals with PCOS for years. I came in January to ask for the referral. I was told that it would be send right away. I expected to wait , because everyone knows the state NHS currently is. But after few months of not hearing anything in regards to fertility treatment I started to push more and more to learn what is going on with my referral only to find out that the referral was not sent at all! I found out about in July after 7 months of waiting for the treatment! Finally,my referral was sent out by the end of July. I still didn’t hear anything about appointment for my treatment so I called Royal Bolton that advised me to ask GP for a letter to speed up my referral. So I made telephone consultation with Dr Khan(the same thy told me he would refer me right away back in January)to ask for it. He said he would issue the letter. recent_reviews.author: Faiz ul Haq
recent_reviews.text: I would like to leave negative feedback regarding Dr. Hussain’s behavior at this surgery. Whenever we ask him for medicine, even for our small children, he always responds by saying: “Go and pick it up from the shelf.” Most recently, my wife, who is pregnant, needed medicine. Whenever she calls, despite the language barrier, Dr. Hussain should at least try to understand that a patient is in need of proper medical advice and prescriptions. Instead, he simply tells her to “get it from the shelf.” I want to ask: if we always have to buy medicine directly from the shelf, then what is the point of having a doctor or a surgery? What role is he fulfilling? During the last call, my wife explained that the medicine he had prescribed previously did not help her at all. She requested an alternative. Instead of listening, Dr. Hussain told her she must not be using the medicine properly. My wife clearly said she knows how to take it, but it was ineffective. At that point, Dr. Hussain disconnected the call and again told her to “buy it from the shelf.” This behavior is extremely unprofessional, dismissive, and rude—especially towards a pregnant woman and parents with small children. A doctor should listen carefully, show empathy, and provide proper medical guidance. Unfortunately, Dr. Hussain’s attitude shows the opposite. I strongly believe that this kind of conduct is unacceptable within the NHS. If doctors are not willing to provide proper medical care and instead simply tell patients to “buy from the shelf,” then they are not fulfilling their responsibility as healthcare providers. I will also be submitting a formal complaint to the NHS regarding this matter. In my opinion, Dr. Hussain should consider retirement, as he does not treat patients with the respect, care, and professionalism that is expected from a doctor.

recent_reviews.text: Over the last few months I have needed a few appointments. To my surprise these appointments have been easy to get. Usually I phone between 8 and 9am, I've been number 1, 2 or 3 in the queue, but, I have still been given an appointment for the same day. For non urgent appointments, these have been offered at alternative times at Moorgate, which is helpful for work purpose. I have seen a few different doctors and each and every one of them has been lovely, efficient and responsive to my needs. They always have time to listen to you and wish you well. I've never felt rushed. The nurses who run the clinics and do bloods etc are so nice, it's good to chat and laugh with them. The office staff are always polite and ready to help if they can. The young man on reception has improved over the last couple of years. It's a good medical centre, though could do with decorating and making it feel a bit more welcoming.

recent_reviews.text: Awful experience this morning at this practice. First of all they thought the best time to do a fire drill would be with a full waiting room and in the freezing cold and rain. Then when we came inside which was 10 minutes after my appointment was meant to be I checked my nhs app to see that my appointment had been changed to 10:45 without my knowledge or notification. There was a reason I booked it at 10:20 not 10:45. I have also never experienced this in the past but I assume it’s so they meet their key performance metrics around access and availability. Some clarity on this would be good and do not blame the fire drill as it was nearly 10 after I should’ve had my appointment when the fire drill was done. Then the nurse I saw basically just fobbed me off when my condition hasn’t improved at all in a week. I have been told to wait another week and come back if it doesn’t improve despite already waiting before I came in to see someone in the first place.

recent_reviews.text: Had to drop off a sample to be sent off and so I arrived at 6pm (half an hour before closing!) and was told they wouldn't take it as samples had already been sent off that day. Furthermore, my condition I've been visiting about causes me unbearable pain which the practice won't even prescribe pain killers for.Like Share Response from the owner a month agoDear Sydney Thank you for taking the time to provide feedback regarding your recent experience at the practice. I am sorry to hear about the distress and frustration this caused you and appreciate the opportunity to respond. My name is Lesley Hyde and I am the Practice Business Manager and part of my role is to monitor and investigate any concerns or complaints made to the practice. Please se below my response to the issues you have raised: Sample Collection Arrangements We apologise for the inconvenience caused when you attended the practice to drop off a sample at 6pm and were advised that it could not be accepted at that time. We understand how frustrating this must have been for you. For clarity, samples must be received by the practice by 4:00pm to ensure they can be included in the scheduled daily laboratory collection at 4:30pm. Samples received after this time cannot be accepted, as they may not be stored within the required conditions and timeframes set by the laboratory. Accepting samples outside of these parameters risks inaccurate or invalid results, which could affect patient care and safety. We do have a poster displayed in our reception area outlining the sample cut off time; however, we acknowledge your feedback that this information may not have been sufficiently visible prior to your visit. As a result of your comments, we have now placed additional signage on our front entrance door and updated our practice website to make sample submission times clearer and more accessible. You can view this update here: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/sample-collection/ Our clinicians usually advise patients of the relevant sample drop off times when issuing sample pots. If this did not occur in your case, we sincerely apologise. We have reminded all clinical and reception staff of the importance of clearly communicating sample cut-off times to patients to help prevent similar situations in the future. Access to the Practice Building We are sorry that you felt unable to re-enter the practice and that this added to your distress. For staff safety reasons, when a receptionist is working alone at the front desk and their colleague is temporarily required elsewhere, the front door may be placed on a buzzer system. In these circumstances, patients are still able to gain access by pressing the buzzer and would be let in by a member of staff. We regret if this was not clear at the time and if it appeared that the practice was closed earlier than advertised. I can assure you however, the practice was still open. Pain Management and Ongoing Care We are sorry to hear about the level of pain you are experiencing. Prescribing decisions, including pain relief, are made by clinicians based on individual clinical assessment and current medical guidance to ensure patient safety. A GP would only prescribe “pain killers” if they felt there was a clinical indication to do so. If your symptoms are persisting, then I would encourage you to arrange a further appointment with a clinician so that your pain and ongoing symptoms can be reviewed again. Next Steps We take all feedback seriously and are grateful that you have brought these matters to our attention, which has already led to improvements in how we share information with patients. If you would like your concerns to be investigated further under the NHS complaints procedure, or if you wish to discuss my response further, please contact me at the practice (0161 226 0606). We are always looking for new members to join our PPG, if you would like further information of if you are interested in joining is, please click the below link: https://www.thearchmedicalpractice.co.uk/practice-information/patient-participation-group/ Yours faithfully Mrs Lesley Hyde Practice Business Manager

recent_reviews.text: Absolutely appalling service – avoid Limelight Health at all costs. I was booked a follow-up telephone consultation three weeks in advance. I stayed in all day from 7am, phone in hand, waiting for the call. Nothing. No call, no missed-call notification, no voicemail. When I rang the surgery, I was told the doctor apparently “called twice and I didn’t answer” – completely untrue. The receptionist refused to investigate, offered no apology, and just said “nothing can be done” and “we’ll just go round in circles”. I now have to start the entire process again and wait weeks more for the appointment I should have had. No accountability, no empathy, and what appears to be a falsified clinical record stating calls were made when they weren’t. Patients are being blamed for the surgery’s failures. Reception staff clearly need urgent training and better systems are needed to stop this kind of thing happening. Deeply unhappy and still without the medical follow-up I need. I do not recommend this practice to anyone.

recent_reviews.author: Liv Zachariasen
recent_reviews.text: Keep dismissing me when I contact them when my toddler is poorly They just refer me to a pharmacy that I can't get to. If I want my toddler to be seen, I have to put through a complaint as it's the only way they'll take me seriously and the last time he turned out to have tonsilitis. My requests on AskmyGP just get closed off with a link to a pharmacy. I was never informed I'd have to be seen by a pharmacy first when I registered at this practice and it has never been communicated. They claim you'll be seen sooner, but before this we've always been sble to be seen on the day. I will never understand fobbing off parents who are worried about their small children and I get this every single time now. I have to always push to be seen and when they finally agree, I'm already so upset and stressed by the whole dismissiveness that I can't be bothered speaking to them. Not sure contacting a GP is supposed to trigger anxiety? It's more than reasonable to not rely on a pharmacy for diagnosis, especially for small children!! The last time he had a fever I didn't even bother contacting them as I couldn't be bothered with the thought of being fobbed off with a pharmacy referral. I get that the NHS is stretched and particularly GP practices, but you should be allowed a consultation every once in a while without a battle. I definitely hope nothing serious ever happens to myself or my family or we better hope the pharmacy can treat us. However having seen the pharmacist as they told me to, I'm none the wiser so what an absolute waste of people's time and energy to pass them round such a useless and inefficient circus. So disappointed as they have resorted to such a lazy way of dealing with their patients.

recent_reviews.author: Oj B
recent_reviews.text: It's so heartbreaking to see this practice degenerate to this level. How hard can it be for people to be nice and professional? They have a lot to do in terms of training all their staff. And I mean ALL of them! From people's skills to civility, mannerisms, tone of voice when addressing patients and how to approach to patients who are already suffering. I've had so many unpleasant encounters with them that I don't want to mention. They make it look like they are doing a favour by attending to you. So appalling! They soon will be having no stars whatsoever if they don't make proper and needed adjustments on their people's skills. It really is appalling! Yelling at patients!! 9/03/2026 I can't believe that I am back here after 4 years to leave a very negative review of this establishment. Before, I go any further - I want to make it clear that, whatever issues patients are having with this medical centre are 90 to 95% front desk, admin, nurses and lesser staff (sorry, for lack of a better word to use.) The Dr's are unaware of the front desk, admin, and lesser staff issues - and yet bear the brunt of the end of the stick should the establishment suffer. I've had very unbelievable and excrutiatingly painful experiences with them from the beginning of this year. In short, (they put up lies and mark your profile, including your number should you call and then mete you undeserved shabby treatment by whoever picks your call, and for whatever reasons best known to them). From the tone of answering your call and how you are responded to is clear and obvious! It is like a syndicate in operation!!! Very evil and unprofessional!!! But we must continue to voice these issues until changes are made, and wrongs are righted. This afternoon I made a call to the centre, having moved to a new home, my daughter who had ran out of medication, due to pressure of moving into a new home and the process of registering with a near gp when settled; called Gorton Medical centre before the weekend to kindly ask for a repeat to be sent to the pharmacy for her to collect. It was not actioned. We called 111 for emergency prescription over the weekend. Today being Monday and on her last tablet, I called the pharmacy to ask if her prescription has come through from the gp, and they said it hadn't. I then called this medical centre to ask why my daughter's prescription had not been actioned and sent to the pharmacy since last week - Knowing she's been on same medication for several years and should not miss days? I was bluntly told by the reception to call back again,(of course, profile marking and syndicate operations in action.)
